steps.why: The question has two halves. The first half is answered by size, one membrane, and the two named examples.
common_mistakes: Writing that microbodies have two membranes. They have one.
Naming only peroxisomes. Glyoxysomes are microbodies too.
steps.memory_tip: Two microbodies, two jobs: peroxisome for peroxide, glyoxysome for fat to sugar.
steps.margin_note: Both names must appear for this mark.

steps.why: Each microbody is named after the reaction it carries out. Peroxisome is named for hydrogen peroxide, glyoxysome for the glyoxylate cycle that turns fat into sugar.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two. Fat to sugar is the glyoxysome.
Writing that microbodies make ATP. That is the mitochondrion.
steps.memory_tip: The name gives the answer: perox-isome breaks peroxide, glyox-ysome runs the glyoxylate cycle.
steps.margin_note: One enzyme job for each body earns this mark.

insider_note: Germinating oil seeds are full of glyoxysomes — that is the example to add if the examiner asks where they occur.
